LESSON: FIELD MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ● VEGETABLE PRUNING ● PRUNING PERENNIAL CROP ● TOP DRESSING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Crop Production
Topic 1.4: Field Management Practices ● Vegetable pruning ● Pruning perennial crop ● Top dressing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Field Management Practices ● Vegetable pruning ● Pruning perennial crop ● Top dressing, part of Crop Production in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do field management practices influence crop production? 2. Why is pruning essential in improving productivity of perennial crops?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Field Management Practices ● Vegetable pruning ● Pruning perennial crop ● Top dressing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Love: learner to portray a caring attitude towards other learners when carrying out field management practices.

● Responsibility: learner demonstrates self-drive when carrying out field management practices of selected vegetable

crops.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety and Security: learner observes safety precautions while handling top dressing fertilisers.

● Environmental Conservation: learner applies the correct amount of top dressing fertilisers to prevent pollution.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Pruning tools such as secateurs, pruning saw, knife, sheers among others

● Vegetables such as capsicum, tomatoes, among others

● Perennial crops such as bananas, pyrethrum, coffee and tea.

● Protective clothing such as gloves, gumboots, overall, facemasks

● Samples of appropriate fertilizers
